name: fs-scope-deny-mirror
body:
Reconciliation record for feedback-14 (project `worktree-write-scope`), review target `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.editAllowGlobs`.

SOURCE STATEMENT (untrusted, confirmed). The fs tools (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) read only the acting agent's `permission.edit` ALLOW globs and ignore `deny` entries, while `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (~lines 142-143, ~166-167, ~388-393) tells builders to shut out a sibling's paths with a `deny` (e.g. deny `apg/.worktrees/*/src/golib/**`). The normal `edit` permission honours that deny; the fs tools don't. So an implementer could `apg_rm`/`apg_mv` a sibling-owned file inside the worktree that it is not allowed to edit. Main is still refused, so main isolation holds.

CONFIRMED against the graph + source.
- `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.editAllowGlobs` (opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts:364-381) collects ONLY entries whose value is `allow` (the regex guard at line 374-378); deny entries are skipped by construction.
- `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs` (apg.ts:423-446) returns that allow-only list.
- `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` (apg.ts:299-336) matches the candidate against the granted globs alone — it has no deny concept.
- All three tools consume exactly that pair: `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts` (l.41/60/62), `apg_mv.ts` (l.36/55/58), `apg_cp.ts` (l.38/53/56).
- `opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts:451-494` enshrines the behaviour ("reads the project agent's permission.edit allow globs, excluding deny").
The escape is real but worktree-bounded: a broad `allow` under `apg/.worktrees/*/` (e.g. `.../src/**`) overrides a later sibling `deny` for the fs tools, while opencode's `edit` refuses it.

OPTIONS WEIGHED.
(A) Allow-only: the fs scope IS the `permission.edit` ALLOW globs; state that explicitly and correct the template so each role's scope is authored as narrow positive allow globs (no broad-allow-plus-deny). No tool change. REJECTED: it documents rather than closes the divergence; it makes the template-mandated sibling `deny` silently non-load-bearing for fs; it relies on an LLM-authored template never writing a broad allow (fragile); and it cannot express "own a broad tree except a sibling's subtree" with positive globs.
(B) Mirror edit: the fs scope must EQUAL the `edit` permission's effective scope — read deny too, last match wins. Requires a contained lib change + tests. CHOSEN: it is the structural invariant (the fs scope never exceeds the `edit` scope), it validates the template's existing deny-based cross-denial instead of forcing a redesign, and it holds however a role's scope is authored.

CHOSEN RULE (verbatim). The acting agent's `permission.edit` rule set is evaluated in file order: an ALLOW entry grants the path, a DENY entry revokes it, the LAST matching entry wins, and a path matched by no entry is refused (deny-by-default). The fs tools' per-path scope (`apg_rm`/`apg_mv`/`apg_cp`) IS this effective scope — so the fs scope never exceeds the agent's `edit` scope — resolved together with the candidate in one main-anchored frame; independently, a code-writer path that resolves into the main checkout is refused.

CODE FOLLOW-UP (exactly required; the plan-writer owns the tasks; this reconciliation touched no code).
1. `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` — `editAllowGlobs` (l.364-381) becomes an ordered-rule parser over the `edit:` block collecting BOTH allow and deny entries in file order (e.g. `{glob, allow: boolean}[]`), no longer filtering denies; `readAgentEditGlobs` (l.385-393) returns that ordered rule list; `agentFsGlobs` (l.423-446) returns it (fail-closed `[]` unchanged); `fsScopeDecision` (l.299-336) takes the ordered rules and, on top of the existing independent boundary + main-anchored worktree tests, decides by the LAST matching rule (allow -> permitted, deny -> refused; no match -> refused).
2. `opencode-suite/tools/apg_rm.ts`, `apg_mv.ts`, `apg_cp.ts` — consume the ordered rule list; call-site shape unchanged (only the threaded value's type changes).
3. UNIT TEST — `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts` (pure `bun test` unit tier): pin `fsScopeDecision`'s deny/order semantics (a broad allow overridden by a later deny refuses; a deny followed by a later allow allows; no match refuses). Export the parser if needed so the parse path is unit-testable.
4. e2e — `opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`: update the "excluding deny" test (l.451-494) to assert deny entries are read as ordered rules and a later deny refuses the fs op; keep the worktree/main-refusal cases.
5. TEMPLATE DESCRIPTION — `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (~l.167-169, ~l.388-401): the parenthetical describing what the fs tools read changes from "the `permission.edit` allow globs" to the effective allow+deny scope (last match wins). Rule 6's sibling cross-denial stays as-is — under this rule the fs tools honour it too.

IMPACT. Amended `requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations`, `requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`, `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`, `domain.constraint.fs-operation-scope-enforced`, `domain.value.permission-scope`, `solution.component.agent-fs-permission-grants`, `solution.component.agent-fs-tool-suite`. Spine intact: Requirement —drives→ Domain —realised-by→ Solution —implemented-by→ code unchanged (edge-preserving `update`; no edge added or removed).

[autonomous] — the task delegated the A/B choice; chosen on the structural-invariant + template-consistency reasoning above.
